block-cast.comment: --[[@as T]] after a value. VS Code's type rule would take the closing ]] as part of a type name and run the comment on into the code after it, so #cast-type colors the type with the same scopes and the rule ends before the first ]], where Lua ends the comment.

leveled-block-cast.comment: --[==[@as T]==], which can hold a ]] as in string[]]==]. The level of the opening brackets is not known here, so any closing brackets with a level end the rule.

cast-type.comment: A type in a block comment, with the scopes VS Code's Lua grammar gives the type of ---@type. A ] is taken one at a time, so the closing brackets stay the comment's.
